what:
Standard workflow for new feature / fast-follow implementations (user preference, always-injected — apply to every code-change task unless user explicitly overrides):

**Before touching code:**
1. **Separate worktree off the active branch** — never implement directly on the active feature branch if other work may be concurrent. Name the branch descriptively (`feature/<phase>-<slug>`).
2. **`git fetch origin` + use latest** as the worktree base — don't branch off a stale local ref.
3. **Confirm the plan** is captured in memory and/or a draft spec before coding, so implementation has a reference.

**During implementation:**
4. **Config-gate new user-facing features** — every new visible behavior needs a knob in the config schema (`defaults.json` + `src/memory/config.ts` if TS-side). Default to "on" / "visible" when the feature helps the user understand what the system is doing, especially in early rollout phases. Users can opt out; they shouldn't have to opt in to basic transparency.
5. **Don't duplicate what the host tool (Claude Code, etc.) already shows.** Surface what's otherwise invisible. Internal accounting (track-* hooks, cleanup operations) stays silent. Soft injections, detections, and auto-actions get surfaced.
6. **Reason text that the agent consumes stays untouched** when adding user-facing reassurance. Use `systemMessage` (user-only channel) for framing. Don't conflate user-facing and agent-facing channels.

**Before shipping:**
7. **Update the product-vision doc** with any directional change. Not just code — reflect the intent shift.
8. **Update the active phase spec doc** with what was actually built (may differ from the spec's original plan).
9. **Update the relevant follow-up doc** (marking items as done, adding new follow-ups discovered).
10. **Update internal docs** (CLAUDE.md equivalents, rules files, developer README).
11. **Update external docs** (public README, any launch material, install docs) if user-visible behavior changed.
12. **Thorough QA: bug audit + unit tests + smoke tests + automated tests. Double/triple-check before declaring done.**

**Reference-by-role, not-by-filename:**
When storing design decisions or workflow memories, reference docs by role — "the active phase spec", "the product-vision doc", "relevant follow-up doc", "internal rules file", "external README", etc. — NOT by exact filename. File names change; roles are stable. This keeps memories from going stale after renames/restructures.

**Deviations from this workflow require explicit user override, not implicit shortcut.**
why: User explicitly asked this be stored as a high-priority preference to bind all future feature work. Captures the entire shape of "how we ship" from workspace setup through testing and docs. Using role-based references instead of exact filenames prevents the memory from going stale. Always-injected so every session starts with this baseline.
